questions.q: What is a dunning procedure?
options: The rulebook for reminders: levels, days, activities and fees
A list of all paid invoices
questions.reason: Each contract account points to a dunning procedure that says how many levels there are, when each starts and what it does.

questions.q: In the example, when does Mette get her first reminder (level 1)?
options: Only after the policy is cancelled
questions.reason: Level 1 starts 14 days after the 15.04 due date, on 29.04, by email and SMS.

questions.q: Does sending a level 1 reminder create a posting document?
options: No, it only saves a dunning history record
questions.reason: No money moves, so there is no posting document. A fee at a later level would create one.

questions.q: What are the two steps of a dunning run?
questions.reason: The proposal (FPVA) builds the list; the activity run (FPVB) sends letters, posts fees and saves history.

questions.q: Which transaction shows the dunning history of a customer?
questions.reason: FPM3 shows which levels a customer reached and when.

questions.q: Mette pays on 06.05, between level 1 and level 2. What happens to dunning?
options: It stops by itself because her items are cleared
questions.reason: Dunning only picks up open, overdue items. Once cleared, the next run ignores her.

questions.q: What is a dunning lock?
options: A 'do not remind' flag on an item or account, often with an end date
A lock on the customer's bank account
A password for the dunning screen
questions.reason: Locks are used for disputes, ongoing investigations or agreed delays.

questions.q: Mette disputes the DKK 100 fee. What should happen?
options: Set a dunning lock on the fee item while it's checked
Send her to a collection agency
questions.reason: Disputed amounts shouldn't be chased; a lock with a reason and end date pauses reminders.

questions.q: Why do dunning procedures have a minimum amount?
options: So tiny debts like DKK 3 don't trigger reminders
questions.reason: A letter can cost more than the debt; small amounts are ignored or written off instead.

questions.q: A return comes back with reason 'bank error'. What is the usual rule?
options: Charge a fee and cancel the policy
questions.reason: It wasn't the customer's fault, so no fee; the debit is tried again.

questions.q: A return comes back with reason 'mandate cancelled'. What should FSCD do?
options: Stop debits and send a bill with a payment slip instead
questions.reason: Future debits would fail too, so the payment method is changed.

questions.q: What does FSCD do first when any return arrives?
options: Reverses the clearing so the item is open again
questions.reason: The payment didn't really happen, so the item must be open again before any other action.

questions.q: What is an instalment plan?
options: Splitting overdue items into smaller amounts with new due dates
A plan to buy more insurance
questions.reason: The original items are parked in the plan; the instalments become the new open items.

questions.q: Mette's DKK 8,188 is split into 3 instalments. Which set adds up correctly?
Which transaction creates an instalment plan?
questions.reason: FPR1 creates an instalment plan in FI-CA based systems.

questions.q: What usually happens after the final notice deadline passes without payment?
options: Cover stops and the policy is cancelled for non-payment
questions.reason: FSCD tells the policy system, which stops cover and works out what's really owed.

questions.q: What does 'write-off' mean?
options: Closing a debt that will never be paid against a bad-debt account
questions.reason: It shows the loss honestly in the books instead of carrying an uncollectable open item.

questions.q: What is 'inkasso' in Denmark?
options: Debt collection by a recovery team or agency
questions.reason: Debt that dunning couldn't collect can be handed to inkasso; FSCD records what was sent and recovered.

questions.q: Which Danish law limits reminder fees and the gap between reminders?
questions.reason: Renteloven caps reminder fees and requires a gap between fee-bearing reminders; always confirm current values with compliance.

questions.q: Under the Insurance Contracts Act, what must the final reminder clearly say?
options: That cover will stop if the premium isn't paid by a stated deadline
questions.reason: The wording of the final notice is a legal requirement, not just a template.

questions.q: Why is e-Boks used for level 2 and 3 letters in Denmark?
options: Digital post is normally treated like a paper letter
It's the only way to send SMS
questions.reason: Most Danish insurers send formal reminders to e-Boks.

questions.q: A customer says 'I never got a reminder'. What is a good first check?
options: Is there a dunning lock, and is the amount above the minimum?
questions.reason: The 'why no reminder?' checklist: overdue? above minimum? locked? in a plan? included in the run? offset by a claim?
